scope: Corollary 5.2 (A finite predictor list) of the manuscript “An L3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform” (preprints/An-L3-bound-for-the-trilinear-Hilbert-transform-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 086 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 24b584066ae76b2f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the two low atoms on J, with complexity at most Hlow. For every B ≥ 1, their product in the form can be replaced, with absolute length-weighted scale-sum error at most e−B poly log(2Dh), 1 + L  ∥1J Fa∥2∥1J Fb∥2, by a finite list of terms ψa(ya)ψb(yb)wI(x, t)e(λ∗t2 ), |λ∗||I|2 ≤ Dpred. (6) The scalar coefficients may depend on the scale. The list of triples (ψa, ψb, λ∗) is fixed on J. Its size, the absolute coefficient bounds, and all atom complexities satisfy log Dpred ≤ poly 1 + B, log(2Hlow)  . The multipliers ψa, ψb may be normalized to have supremum norm at most one by incorporating their sizes into the coefficients.
